messages.subject: [aroma.affymetrix] Crash in fit(plm)
parts:
Hi

I am a total newbie with  R analysis and this is my first analysis I am doing with Aroma.
I am getting the same error repetitively after following instruction on the project website.
I have the last R version (R 2.14.1) and last Aroma version (2.4.0). I am running under windows seven.

I have done 6 arrays MoGene-1_0-st-v1, 3 replicate and 2 conditions. I have followed the instruction for the filename, paths and I download the binary CDF from Aroma as well. Moreover, I deactivated Buffer output.

Here is my code:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
path <- "C:\\Users\\jean-paul\\Desktop\\projectA"
setwd(path)
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8, timestamp=TRUE)
chipType <- "MoGene-1_0-st-v1"
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType(chipType, tags="r3")

## not very useful but I would like to get Ensembl Transcript ID later ##
csv <- AffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile$byChipType(chipType, tags="")

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("msc", cdf=cdf)
bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
plm <- RmaPlm(csN)

### Crash at this step ####
fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
### Crash at this step ####


Here is my sessionInfo()
> sessionInfo()
R version 2.14.1 (2011-12-22)
Platform: i386-pc-mingw32/i386 (32-bit)

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=French_Switzerland.1252  LC_CTYPE=French_Switzerland.1252  
[3] LC_MONETARY=French_Switzerland.1252 LC_NUMERIC=C                      
[5] LC_TIME=French_Switzerland.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base    

other attached packages:
 [1] aroma.affymetrix_2.4.0 affxparser_1.26.2      aroma.apd_0.2.0      
 [4] R.huge_0.3.0           aroma.core_2.4.5       aroma.light_1.22.0    
 [7] matrixStats_0.4.3      R.rsp_0.7.1            R.cache_0.6.1        
[10] R.filesets_1.1.4       digest_0.5.1           R.utils_1.9.11        
[13] R.oo_1.8.3             R.methodsS3_1.2.1    

I cannot do traceback() because R freezes completely.
Thanks in advance for your help

Jean-Paul Abbuehl
EPFL, Switzerland

they occur instead of getting them all at the end (or in chunks).

>

> verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8, timestamp=TRUE)

>

>
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("msc", cdf=cdf)
> bc <- RmaBackgroundCorrection(cs)
> csBC <- process(bc,verbose=verbose)
> qn <- QuantileNormalization(csBC, typesToUpdate="pm")
> csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose)
> plm <- RmaPlm(csN)
>
> ### Crash at this step ####
> fit(plm, verbose=verbose)
> ### Crash at this step ####

You may already know this, but some important clarification about the
R terminology, which, if used when reporting issues here and to the R
help and the Bioconductor help mailing lists, simplifies the
troubleshooting:

- Warnings and errors: R generates warnings and errors. Errors often
stops the running of your scripts/code, whereas warnings are less
severe and are only reported as messages.
- Crashes/core dumps: When people talk about crashes (or core dumps in
the Unix world), they mean that something really severe happened
causing R to simply die and shutdown by itself without user
interaction.
- Hangs/freezes: This is used when R no longer responds even when the
user tries to interrupt/stop the script.

So, above you write that fit(plm, verbose=verbose) "crash" and below
"freeze". It sounds like you are saying that R is non-responsive. Is
that correct? If so, have you tried to press Ctrl-C (one or several
times) at this stage? If that interrupts R and brings you back to the
prompt, everything is fine. If it doesn't, I have more concerns and
we have to do some serious troubleshooting, because it is never good
when R/aroma truly "freezes".

Now, if you can interrupts R at this stage by pressing Ctrl-C, I'd say
things works as expected. What instead happens is that it takes a
really long time (5-30 minutes) to do a particular internal step,
namely the creating of what is called the "monocell CDF". See 'FAQ.
2007-02-13: Why is aroma.affymetrix slow?'
[http://aroma-project.org/faq/] and you'll understand why you need to
be patient the very first time you use aroma.

You can see that things do actually work by displaying more "verbose"
output, e.g.

fit(plm, verbose=-10)

or even

fit(plm, verbose=-50)

Let me know if this explained your issues

/Henrik
